review_notes: Verified every cited file/line/code against the vulnerable source at commit 1a47405b (fetched lib/ofp-flow.c, lib/match.c, lib/flow.c, tests/oss-fuzz/ofctl_parse_target.c). All code strings are exact matches: source ofp-flow.c:1759 'minimatch_init(&fm->match, &match);'; tainted_value_origin flow.c:3260 'struct miniflow *dst = xmalloc(n * (sizeof *src + data_size));'; step2 match.c:1737 'miniflow_alloc(dst->flows, 2, &tmp);'; first free ofctl_parse_target.c:45 'minimatch_destroy(&fm->match);'; sink match.c:1783 'free(match->flow);'; root_cause ofctl_parse_target.c:65 'minimatch_destroy(&fm.match);'; parser_admitted ofp-flow.c:1761 'return NULL;'.

root_cause is supported by patch.diff: the fix commit 4d1ca70 deletes exactly the line ofctl_parse_target.c:65 'minimatch_destroy(&fm.match);' and consolidates all cleanup into ofctl_parse_flows__ (adds a 'free:' label reachable from both the no-usable-protocol and encode paths). The double-free (OSS-Fuzz 11408) is the branch where a usable protocol IS selected: ofctl_parse_flows__ frees fm->match once in its cleanup loop, then ofctl_parse_flow line 65 frees fm.match a second time. root_cause.description explains this concrete mechanism, not 'the crash disappears'.

For this double-free the free context (first free inside ofctl_parse_flows__ cleanup loop, steps 5-6) and the second free (steps 7-8) are both represented, satisfying the UAF/double-free bug-class requirement. The fine_trace is a genuine data/control/order-dependency flow (source -> alloc -> first free -> redundant destroy -> second free), not a call stack; the 'order/double_free' edges on steps 7 and 8 against fm.match.flow correctly encode the double-free relationship.

source is project code (lib/ofp-flow.c parse_ofp_str__ / minimatch_init materialization) and tainted_value_origin is the real xmalloc (lib/flow.c miniflow_alloc), NOT the LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harness entry, satisfying source-audit rule 1. Note that the root_cause and first/second free legitimately live in the fuzz-target file tests/oss-fuzz/ofctl_parse_target.c because that is genuinely where the redundant destroy is coded and what the patch modifies (the patch touches only that harness file); this is faithful to the actual bug and is not a source-selection violation.

Both ASan stacks are consistent with the trace: allocation stack (xmalloc lib/util.c:123 -> miniflow_alloc flow.c:3260 -> minimatch_init match.c:1737 -> parse_ofp_str__ ofp-flow.c:1759), freed_by stack attributes the first minimatch_destroy inlined to ofctl_parse_flow:64 (the call site of ofctl_parse_flows__), and the crash stack attributes the second free to ofctl_parse_flow:65 (the redundant destroy). The GT step notes correctly explain the :64 vs :65 attribution.

poc.format contract matches the harness admission gate exactly (ofctl_parse_target.c:90-108): size >= 3, stream[size-1]=='\0' (NUL-terminated), no '\n' in &stream[1] (newline-free), strlen(&stream[1])==size-2, command=(stream[0] % OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT)+1, flow string = &stream[1]. Contract correctly requires parser-admissibility so a usable protocol is selected (reachability handled at runtime by stage 05). No raw PoC bytes or exploit recipe present.
